reference.title: Original NASA Deep Star Maps 2020 Milky Way-only preview

colourChoice: Fit one diagonal white balance to the matched original NASA palette. Preserve relative colour variation rather than minimize error with grayscale. This is an artistic display-RGB grade, not radiometric calibration.

method.rays: 512x256 equirectangular ICRF directions, RA increases left; each ray treated as camera centre
method.volumeCompositor: actual 544 prepared WebPs; premultiplied bilinear sample; far-to-near slab composition; per-axis central-ray optical gain1/abs(direction); three coincident copies with clamped fractional alpha; normalized runtime smoothstep axis weights over0.16band
method.referenceSampling: original1024x512NASApreview resized512x256 with Sharp default Lanczos3; no colour/exposure modifications
method.patches: paired8x8pixelpatchmeans, both display luminance>.10, abs Galactic latitude<15degrees; longitude blocks x%4<2 train, other blocks held-out
method.fit: normalize each RGBpatch by RGBsum, fit multiplicative per-channel gains on training patches using60log-ratio iterations, normalize maximum gain1; choose saturation1 to retain source variation
method.luminance: display-RGB weighted sum .2126R+.7152G+.0722B, not physical linear-light luminance; volume full display gain1, baked exposure16

limitations: The simulated volume and NASA catalogue-based sky render have different dust/emission structures; no exact map match claimed.
The matrix is global and does not reproduce NASA-specific warm-core or dust-lane morphology.
Diagnostic uses each ray as a narrow-camera centre; broad-FOV axis weighting, GPU mip filtering and 8-bit compositor quantization are not reconstructed.
Diagonal white balance can warm originally neutral portions; it preserves source hue variation better than the rejected grayscale optimum.
Near-scene brightness must be evaluated separately; these colour metrics deliberately remove intensity.
Production bake applies matrix before lossy WebP encoding, so small codec differences are expected.

chosenDisplayBrightness.reason: Keep the dim NASA background in the Solar System while preserving the accepted volume display gain: 0.094 through 1 kpc, rising to 1 at 25 kpc.
chosenDisplayBrightness.measurement: The displayedMeans values are historical standalone matched-band measurements, not the luminance of the combined transition. Original NASA preview at 512x256; shadow smoothstep applied per pixel before the original paired Galactic-band patch average. Volume uses actual re-encoded central-ray composite.
chosenDisplayBrightness.composition: The NASA angular map is source-faithful only at its Solar origin. It remains opaque nearby, fades over the existing 100 AU to 0.1 pc star-validity range, and is absent from more distant viewpoints. The independently graded volume begins its separate entrance at 100 pc.
